content:
maya: FYI seeing a couple of high-priority customer escalations for Dedicated in ap-southeast1 — placement failures + repeated 429 throttles. acme_ai and boldlabs have active incidents.
raj: can you paste the error snippets? 429 from our gateway or upstream?
maya: gateway returns 429 'throttled by placement' and scheduler logs show 'no suitable GPU available' + some autoscaler churn. attaching quick logs below.
sasha: omg noisy neighbor reports earlier today, we had one host with runaway memory growth. could be impacting packing.
maya: logs:
```
2026-03-16T02:12:05Z scheduler ERROR placement failed: NoCompatibleDevice
2026-03-16T02:12:06Z autoscaler INFO scale_down start: candidate_nodes=3
2026-03-16T02:12:08Z gateway WARN request_id=abc123 status=429 reason=placement_throttle
```
kevin: are these Dedicated pools pinned to ap-southeast1 only? or do customers allow multi-region failover?
lisa_support: acme_ai has region_lock: true in their contract. Boldlabs allowed failover but prefers same region for latency. both flagged as P1.
raj: ok immediate actions: 1) check available GPU inventory in ap-southeast1 2) hold any scale-downs 3) identify noisy neighbor host and migrate workloads 4) notify customers with ETA
sasha: I'm on noisy-host hunt — running `kubectl describe pod` on suspected nodes and checking nvidia-smi for weird memory usage.
kevin: I'll flip autoscaler to conservative mode for that availability zone (min_replicas = current) and disable aggressive binpacking for 15m.
maya: deploy-bot: trigger capacity snapshot? @deploy-bot can we get current pool utilization + pending queue?
deploy-bot: capacity_snapshot: ap-southeast1: total_gpus=320, allocated=315, pending_requests=28, reserved_dedicated=40
raj: 315/320 with 28 pending — pretty tight, plus reserved leads to oversubscription for unreserved requests.
lisa_support: customers reporting higher latency (p95 generation increased from 120ms -> 520ms) and some 500s. sending customers the workaround: switch to hosted fallback or route to eu-west1 if acceptable.
sasha: found a host with 4 of 8 GPUs stuck at ~95% mem due to a hung process from container coredump. evicting and reprovisioning now.
kevin: eviction may free 3 GPUs, but still short ~25 for queued. Could we temporarily allow bursting to Dedicated GPU pool from shared host pool?
raj: we have a pre-approved emergency burst policy but needs manual approval for region-level. pinging ops-lead for signoff.
maya: note: billing teams flagged some customers for suspiciously high sustained concurrency — possible runaway loops. need CS to confirm it's intended.
lisa_support: contacting acme_ai to confirm. they say they kicked off a large eval job accidentally and will cancel within 10m.
deploy-bot: autoscaler action: scale_up 6 nodes requested (ETA ~3m)
kevin: scaling in-flight, flipping binpack to spread to avoid single host overload. also enabling prefix KV cache to reduce generation token cost for pending customers.
sasha: evict + reprovision done on noisy host. freed 3 GPUs.
raj: new snapshot?
deploy-bot: capacity_snapshot: ap-southeast1: total_gpus=326, allocated=318, pending_requests=12, reserved_dedicated=40
maya: pending down from 28 -> 12. Good. still need to monitor for placement failures.
lisa_support: updated acme_ai: told them we have started scaling, suggested temporary hosted fallback, they accepted hosted fallback for 30m.
kevin: added a hotfix to scheduler: prefer spread placement over tight pack for the next 10m to avoid noisy neighbor reoccurrence. patch id: hotfix-587
raj: followups: - confirm autoscaler completed scale_up - run root-cause for noisy host crash - review reservation vs soft quota to avoid future oversubscribe - ops-lead to sign emergency burst policy for ap-southeast
sasha: collecting kernel/pod logs from noisy host, uploading to incident bucket.
maya: thanks all. happy path: scale finished and customers on fallback -> no more 429s. Will keep thread open for RCA notes. :thumbsup:
kevin: update 10m later — no new 429s, p95 back to ~140ms for affected customers. marking incident as mitigated.
maya: leaving summary for postmortem: cause = oversubscription combined with noisy-host memory leak + one large accidental customer run. mitigations applied: autoscaler conservative mode, hotfix for spread placement, eviction of noisy host, temporary hosted fallback. next steps: quota policy change and reservation auditing.
raj: adding incident owner: maya. please open postmortem ticket.
lisa_support: customers notified and satisfied. closing loop. :white_check_mark:
